original_value: A method for automatic compensation of misalignment angles during matching the scale factors of two pairs of the accelerometers in developing the rotating accelerometer gravity gradient instrument (GGI) is proposed and demonstrated in this paper. The purpose of automatic scale factor matching of the four accelerometers in GGI is to suppress the common mode acceleration of the moving-based platforms. However, taking the full model equation of the accelerometer into consideration, the other two orthogonal axes which is the pendulous axis and the output axis, will also sense the common mode acceleration and reduce the suppression performance. The coefficients from the two axes to the output are δO and δP respectively, called the misalignment angles. The angle δO, coupling with the acceleration along the pendulous axis perpendicular to the rotational plane, will not be modulated by the rotation and gives little contribution to the scale factors matching. On the other hand, because of coupling with the acceleration along the centripetal direction in the rotating plane, the angle δP would produce a component with 90 degrees phase delay relative to the scale factor component. Hence, the δP component coincides exactly with the sensitive direction of the orthogonal accelerometers. To improve the common mode acceleration rejection, the misalignment angle δP is compensated by injecting a trimming current, which is proportional to the output of an orthogonal accelerometer, into the torque coil of the accelerometer during the scale factor matching. The experimental results show that the common linear acceleration suppression achieved three orders after the scale factors balance and five orders after the misalignment angles compensation, which is almost down to the noise level of the used accelerometers of 1~2 × 10−7 g/√Hz (1 g ≈ 9.8 m/s2).

result.paraphrase: This paper proposes and demonstrates an automatic method for compensating misalignment angles while matching the scale factors of two accelerometer pairs in a rotating accelerometer gravity gradient instrument (GGI). Automatic scale-factor matching for all four GGI accelerometers is intended to suppress common-mode acceleration on the moving base platforms. However, when the full accelerometer model is considered, the other two orthogonal axes—the pendulous axis and the output axis—also sense common-mode acceleration, which degrades suppression. Their coupling coefficients to the output are δO and δP, respectively, and are referred to as misalignment angles. The angle δO, which couples with acceleration along the pendulous axis perpendicular to the rotation plane, is not modulated by rotation and contributes little to scale-factor matching. In contrast, δP couples with acceleration along the centripetal direction in the rotating plane and produces a component with a 90-degree phase lag relative to the scale-factor component. As a result, the δP term aligns exactly with the sensitive direction of the orthogonal accelerometers. To enhance common-mode acceleration rejection, δP is compensated during scale-factor matching by injecting a trimming current into the accelerometer torque coil, proportional to the output of an orthogonal accelerometer. Experimental results indicate that common linear acceleration suppression reaches three orders of magnitude after scale factors are balanced and five orders of magnitude after misalignment-angle compensation, nearly down to the used accelerometers’ noise level of 1~2 × 10−7 g/√Hz (1 g ≈ 9.8 m/s2).
